- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing filter or cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per period if recent 5-day avg is below 30-day avg.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misreads sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns from negative to neutral/positive within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day high, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., 0.5x sentiment value as % correction).
